submitter: deferred_work_item_park lane (bugs_open/396) - ROUND 1, the park verb
rationale:
bugs_open/396. Four lanes each needed to hold a site's work queue still while rebuilding that site. The platform offers NO verb for that, so each improvised the same hand-written UPDATE at a psql prompt, and only the lanes that thought of it left a trace. 52 rows fleet-wide are now parked at status='deferred' with a named handler_agent and NO provenance of any kind; 62 more are parked with provenance, in three DIFFERENT hand-invented shapes.

The cost is not theoretical. 'deferred' is selected by nothing (claim_work_item_action.go:102 claims status IN ('triaged','approved'); the promoter takes status='detected') AND it is absent from idx_swi_dedup's exclusion list, so a parked row still holds its (site_id,item_key) slot. On 2026-08-25 one such row - a page_rerender parked 2026-08-03, attempt_count 0, 22 days old - blocked bugs_open/328's dispatch for that page with a 23505 that reads as 'already queued' and means 'queued and abandoned'. Re-armed by hand to 'triaged', it completed in 2 minutes and the page then served correctly.

THIS IS A MISSING VERB, NOT A BROKEN WRITER, and that is the load-bearing claim I am asking you to test. No Go path produces the bad shape: there is no `UPDATE site_work_items ... SET status='deferred'` anywhere in platform/, internal/, pkg/ or cmd/, and all six Go writers of that status pair it with HandlerAgent: "" deliberately and with comments. A recursive walk over every agent_definitions row (snapshots and deleted included) finds exactly ONE step fleet-wide configured with status 'deferred', and it carries an empty handler. So the rows are made by PEOPLE, which is why the remedy has to be reachable by people - at a psql prompt, which is where all four parks were performed. A Go action would not have been called by any of them, and that is the reason this ships as a SQL function rather than a registered action.

THE STRUCTURAL PROPERTY: p_parked_by, p_parked_reason and p_release_condition have NO DEFAULTS. The stamp is unskippable because it is an ARGUMENT, not a habit. That is the whole fix; everything else is guardrails.

I am NOT proposing to un-park anything, and unpark_work_items is deliberately scoped to a single p_parked_by: 60 currently-parked rows carry another lane's LIVE release condition ('un-park after rebuild verify'), and a blanket release would fire real dispatches onto live customer sites.

plan.summary: Ship a park verb as two SQL functions in migration 621, so that holding a site's queue becomes a supported, self-documenting act instead of a hand-written UPDATE that records nothing. park_work_items() cannot be called without who/why/release-condition (no defaults on those three parameters); its unsafe side is OFF by default (p_apply DEFAULT false, so a bare call is a dry run); it refuses a NULL site, an unknown site, a blank reason, a claimed row, a terminal row, and any candidate set larger than p_max_rows. unpark_work_items() restores each row to the status recorded per-row at park time and will only release rows carrying the caller's own p_parked_by. Stamps go in `result`, NOT `spec`, because refreshOpenWorkItem replaces spec wholesale on re-detection. Every refusal is INDUCED in the migration's own DO-block guard, with a positive control (a well-formed dry run must succeed and return applied=false) and a negative control (the dry run must have written nothing).

edits.rationale: The verb itself. A SQL function rather than a Go action because the measured users are sessions at a psql prompt - all four recorded parks were performed that way, and a registered action would not have been called by any of them. It is also live on apply with no image roll, which matters because the alternative people currently reach for is one UPDATE statement.
edits.sketch: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION park_work_items(p_site_id uuid, p_parked_by text, p_parked_reason text, p_release_condition text, p_item_types text[] DEFAULT NULL, p_exclude_ids uuid[] DEFAULT NULL, p_max_rows integer DEFAULT 50, p_apply boolean DEFAULT false) RETURNS jsonb -- first four have NO defaults, so the stamp cannot be skipped. Parkable statuses are ('triaged','approved','detected') ONLY: never 'claimed' (a handler may be acting on the row now) and never a terminal status (parking a closed row would resurrect it into idx_swi_dedup's kept set and block re-filing). UPDATE ... SET status='deferred', result = COALESCE(result,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('parked_by',...,'parked_reason',...,'parked_from_status', w.status,'parked_at',...,'release_condition',...,'parked_by_verb','park_work_items') FROM _park_candidates c WHERE w.id=c.id AND w.status=c.status -- the trailing status match is a lost-update guard: anything that moved under us is skipped and reported as raced_and_skipped rather than silently overwritten.

edits.rationale: unpark, in the same file. Scoped to one p_parked_by on purpose - this is the guard that stops a well-meaning session releasing a hold somebody else is deliberately maintaining. It restores each row to the status recorded FOR THAT ROW at park time, so a mixed batch (triaged + detected) comes back correctly rather than being flattened to one status.
edits.sketch: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION unpark_work_items(p_site_id uuid, p_parked_by text, p_max_rows integer DEFAULT 200, p_apply boolean DEFAULT false) RETURNS jsonb -- candidates are status='deferred' AND result->>'parked_by' = p_parked_by AND result ? 'parked_from_status'. REFUSES if any candidate's parked_from_status is outside ('triaged','approved','detected') rather than guessing. On apply: SET status = c.restore_to, and strip the six park keys from result while adding unparked_at/unparked_by.

edits.rationale: The guard block. The estate's rule is that a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT (ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result), so this is DO/RAISE - and every refusal is INDUCED rather than asserted to exist, because a guard nobody has watched fail is a guard you are assuming.
edits.sketch: DO $guard$ ... five BEGIN/EXCEPTION blocks that each CALL the function with a bad argument and RAISE if it was ACCEPTED (blank parked_by; blank release_condition; NULL site; unknown site; unpark with blank parked_by), counting v_fired and requiring v_fired = 5. Then a POSITIVE CONTROL - a well-formed dry run must return applied=false and include would_park, because five refusals are otherwise equally consistent with a function that refuses everything. Then a NEGATIVE CONTROL - no row may carry parked_by='guard-test', proving the dry run wrote nothing. Tested by running the whole file with COMMIT replaced by ROLLBACK: 5 refusals induced, plan returned, nothing written, nothing left behind.

edits.rationale: Drops both functions and deliberately does NOT un-park anything - rows parked through the verb are stamped and can be released by their holder with a considered decision, whereas a blanket release here would fire real dispatches onto live customer sites. States how to release by hand from the stamps if the rollback is because the verb misbehaved.
edits.sketch: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.park_work_items(uuid,text,text,text,text[],uuid[],integer,boolean); DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.unpark_work_items(uuid,text,integer,boolean); + a DO/RAISE guard asserting both are absent afterwards.

edits.rationale: Registered in the SAME COMMIT that ships it, per the owner ruling of 2026-07-28 condition (2) - a seam registered 'later' is how a seam becomes folklore. Another lane could call this and would not otherwise know it exists.
edits.sketch: New WII-nnn entry beside the 33 existing ones, naming both functions, the required-argument property that makes the stamp unskippable, the result-not-spec rationale (refreshOpenWorkItem replaces spec wholesale), the induced-guard evidence, and the explicit NON-GOAL: it does not and must not release another lane's hold. Index count in 000_concept_index.md updated; any matching 102_coverage_ratchet.txt line dropped.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] the deferred population, computed with a GROUP BY over a CASE: 303 total = 87 spec.parked_by (migration 389) + 4 spec.deferred_reason + 63 result.deferred_by/deferred_at + 105 empty-handler roadmap rows + 52 with no stamp in EITHER jsonb column.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] of those 52: 0 carry handled_by, 0 carry error, 0 have attempt_count > 0. CONTROL proving the instrument works: handled_by is populated on 7,114 of 7,329 'complete' rows, so the zero is a real absence and not a dead column.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] no Go path writes the shape: `grep -rn -A4 'UPDATE site_work_items' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/ | grep -E 'status *= *\$'` returns three parameterised writers - two on the sites table, and FailWorkItemAction's status_override. FailWorkItemAction is excluded because it stamps handled_by = agentType and 0 of the 52 carry it.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] recursive walk over every agent_definitions row including snapshots and deleted: exactly ONE live step is configured with status 'deferred' (improvement-loop/create_work_item, capability_gap, EMPTY handler), and ZERO carry status_override='deferred'. A source grep could not have cleared these config-driven doors; the config walk is the evidence.

The six competing ad-hoc conventions the absence of a verb has produced: spec.parked_by (migration 389), spec.deferred_reason (canary_replan_407), spec.not_dispatchable (remit.go), result.deferred_by/-_reason/-_from_status (loancalculator_rebuild_thread, apis-uk-bees-lane), result.repair_284 (migration 442), and a reason appended to created_by.

migration 389_park_contrast_failures_and_reenable_improvement_sweep.sql is the estate's own model for a good park and is where the stamp field names come from: a precondition that RAISE EXCEPTIONs if the premise is gone, spec.parked_from_status/parked_reason/parked_by, GET DIAGNOSTICS asserted against a pre-count, and a negative control proving nothing else moved.

archive_completed_work_items(min_age_days, batch_limit) RETURNS jsonb, already live in pg_proc on this same table - the sibling whose shape (plpgsql, parameterised with defaults, temp candidate table, GET DIAGNOSTICS, jsonb summary) this function deliberately mirrors rather than inventing a new one.
